gate1RoundTrip.description: PLAN.md Phase 1 Gate 1 verification: mint 100 basket tokens from real ATS GOLD-x/STOCK-x, redeem back to the exact original balances (10000/10000, zero dust).

gate2DepositWithdraw.description: PLAN.md Phase 2 Gate 2, deposit/withdraw leg: deposit 100 GOLD-x directly into the raw pool, withdraw it back out, balances exact.

gate2BorrowRepay.description: PLAN.md Phase 2 Gate 2, borrow/repay leg - full gate now passed. Unblocked by the Pyth -> Chainlink oracle pivot (see docs/phase-2-findings.md): getUserAccountData, borrow, and repay all need a live oracle price, which StratusChainlinkPriceOracle provides directly (push-based, no update step). Borrowed ~50% of available capacity against 100 GOLD-x collateral, repaid in full - USDC balance and total debt returned to exactly the pre-borrow state, health factor computed correctly throughout (2.14 mid-borrow, MAX after repay).

gate3DecomposeRecompose.description: PLAN.md Phase 3 Gate 3, deposit/decompose + withdraw/recompose legs: depositBasket(50) decomposes into 25 GOLD-x + 25 STOCK-x, each aToken balance increases independently (BasketDecomposed event); withdrawing both from the pool and calling recomposeBasket(50) returns exactly 50 basket tokens (BasketRecomposed event). Borrow leg is mechanically identical to gate2BorrowRepay above (the vault never touches borrowing) - now unblocked the same way.

oraclePivot.description: Pyth (StratusPriceOracle) is blocked by infrastructure outside this repo's control - see docs/phase-2-findings.md. The pool is wired to StratusChainlinkPriceOracle instead, backed by real, live, push-based Chainlink feeds on Hedera testnet. GOLD-x -> HBAR/USD, STOCK-x -> ETH/USD (same honest substitution pattern as the original Pyth design), USDC -> USDC/USD.

gate4LiquidationPrimary.description: PLAN.md Phase 4 Gate 4, primary scenario: deposited value-balanced GOLD-x (~$718) and STOCK-x (~$742) directly into the pool, borrowed 90% of combined capacity, stressed GOLD-x -90% via StratusChainlinkPriceOracle.setDemoOffsetBps (DEMO-ONLY, see PLAN.md §6.3), health factor dropped to 0.65, liquidator (a distinct funded/whitelisted account, not the borrower) called liquidationCall(GOLD-x, USDC, ...) - seized all available GOLD-x collateral (it was worth less than the covered debt even with the liquidation bonus). STOCK-x aToken balance confirmed byte-for-byte unchanged (0.3 before and after).

gate4LiquidationMirror.description: PLAN.md Phase 4 Gate 4, mirror scenario (per PLAN.md: 'so the isolation claim isn't a one-asset fluke'): same mechanism, STOCK-x/ETH stressed -60% instead of GOLD-x/HBAR, liquidator seized STOCK-x only. GOLD-x aToken balance confirmed byte-for-byte unchanged (800.0 before and after).

demoStateCleanup.description: Reset to a clean slate after the Gate 4 mirror run (contracts/script/cleanup-demo-state.ts) - neither liquidation demo script cleans up after itself on purpose. Repaid all outstanding debt and cleared STOCK-x's leftover demo stress, so the deployment is ready to re-record from a healthy state (collateral $267.09, debt $0, health factor MAX).

riskViewOracleFix.description: StratusRiskView's `oracle` is immutable and was still pointed at the dead Pyth-backed StratusPriceOracle from before the oraclePivot (see that meta entry) - the pool itself moved to Chainlink, but RiskView's own getAssetPrice() call kept hitting Pyth and reverting with StalePrice() (selector 0x19abf40e), surfaced in the frontend as an unreadable 'unknown custom error' on every Deposit/Risk Panel page load. Redeployed StratusRiskView (read-only, no state) against StratusChainlinkPriceOracle via contracts/script/redeploy-risk-view.ts; getUserRisk() now succeeds on-chain with no revert. Old, broken address was 0x05aD00333d8bf0C920F0041770344182c54f37c4.

redstoneOracleIntegration.description: Real RWA price feeds via RedStone's pull oracle model (redstone-primary-prod data service) - GOLD-x tracks real gold (XAU), STOCK-x tracks the real S&P 500 index (USA500.Y), USDC tracks real USDC/USD. Closes the disclosed-substitute gap in StratusChainlinkPriceOracle/StratusPriceOracle (which mapped GOLD-x/STOCK-x to HBAR/ETH since no RWA feed was live on Hedera testnet from Chainlink, Supra, or blocked Pyth - see docs/phase-3-oracle-research.md for the full research trail, including 3 real bugs found in RedStone's own published package). Architecture: updatePrice(asset) is a permissionless function that must be called via a RedStone-wrapped transaction (calldata carries a signed price payload) and caches {price, timestamp}; getAssetPrice(asset), the IPriceOracleGetter-facing function everything else calls, is a plain view read of that cache - so StratusRiskView/LendingPool/frontend needed no RedStone-specific changes. Prices only refresh when script/update-redstone-prices.ts runs (pull/cache, not continuous push) - a real ongoing operational requirement, run before any demo.

individualStockReserves.description: 10 individual real-stock reserves added alongside (not replacing) the original GOLD-x/STOCK-x basket - AAPL-x, TSLA-x, MSFT-x, NVDA-x, GOOGL-x, AMZN-x, META-x, BRKB-x, AMD-x, PLTR-x. Each is its own ATS Equity token, its own pool reserve (aToken/debtToken/interest rate strategy via batchInitReserve, chunked into groups of 3 - 11-at-once exceeded Hedera's per-tx gas limit), whitelisted (LendingPool + its own aToken) on its own ATS control list, and wired to a real RedStone price feed. Collateral-enabled, no borrowing (LTV 50%/threshold 60%/bonus 10%). An 11th candidate, CVX (intended as Chevron), was dropped after its returned price ($2.21) turned out to be Convex Finance's crypto token, not Chevron stock - caught by sanity-checking the value, not just the ticker name; see docs/phase-4-individual-stocks.md and tokenization/config/individual-stocks.json. Real deposit/withdraw verified end-to-end for AAPL-x (balances restored exactly).
individualStockReserves.cvxTickerCollisionNote: CvxToken/InterestRateStrategy_CVX-x/aToken_CVX-x exist in this file's contracts section (real on-chain infra, deployed before the collision was caught) but are unused and not referenced by tokenization/config/individual-stocks.json, the oracle price-refresh script, or the frontend.
